chapters.title: Introduction
chapters.sourcePressure: The frame chapter argues that motives hide beneath stories, self-love distorts self-knowledge, social life rewards masks, and the first honest subject is yourself.
chapters.coreMove: Separate observable behavior, motive story, and repeated pattern before judging anyone, starting with your own blindness.
chapters.commonMisread: Turning the opening into a generic warning that people are complicated instead of a disciplined method for reading motives while auditing yourself.

chapters.title: Master Your Emotional Self: The Law of Irrationality
chapters.sourcePressure: This law says emotion directs judgment before reason narrates it, so rationality starts by catching biases, inflaming factors, and the delayed arrival of the calmer self.
chapters.coreMove: Name the emotional surge, delay action, and rebuild the sequence before reason turns the surge into a respectable story.
chapters.commonMisread: Making this a call to suppress feelings or be calm rather than a concrete practice for interrupting emotional certainty.

chapters.title: Transform Self-Love into Empathy: The Law of Narcissism
chapters.sourcePressure: This law treats narcissism as a spectrum and asks the reader to turn some self-love into empathy instead of using narcissism as an insult.
chapters.coreMove: Redirect attention from your own image and hurt toward the other person's inner pressure before deciding what they owe you.
chapters.commonMisread: Using narcissism as a label for bad people instead of recognizing the ordinary pull of self-absorption in yourself.

chapters.title: See Through People's Masks: The Law of Role-playing
chapters.sourcePressure: This law says social life runs on performance, and insight comes from reading masks, second language, and the gap between polished presentation and repeated conduct.
chapters.coreMove: Read the role a person needs to perform, then compare their second language and repeated behavior with the mask.
chapters.commonMisread: Reducing masks to lying instead of seeing ordinary performance, self-protection, and unconscious role needs.

chapters.title: Determine the Strength of People's Character: The Law of Compulsive Behavior
chapters.sourcePressure: This law replaces charisma-based judgment with slower pattern recognition: character shows through recurring compulsions under stress, frustration, dependence, and time.
chapters.coreMove: Test character by repeated behavior under pressure, dependence, and frustration rather than by talent, apology, or charm.
chapters.commonMisread: Making character a moral vibe instead of a trackable pattern of compulsive behavior.

chapters.title: Become an Elusive Object of Desire: The Law of Covetousness
chapters.sourcePressure: This law argues desire intensifies around distance, scarcity, projection, and rivalry wherever status, attention, opportunity, or possession feels contested.
chapters.coreMove: Shape desire by withholding complete access, creating room for projection, and refusing to beg for attention.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating covetousness as manipulation or romance only, instead of understanding how distance and scarcity structure wanting.

chapters.title: Elevate Your Perspective: The Law of Shortsightedness
chapters.sourcePressure: This law makes time horizon the issue: anger, vanity, panic, revenge, and excitement collapse the future into the present moment.
chapters.coreMove: Step outside immediate emotional reward and price the decision against its delayed cost and future position.
chapters.commonMisread: Calling this patience or long-term thinking in general rather than catching the exact present-moment force that shrinks perspective.

chapters.title: Soften People's Resistance by Confirming Their Self-Opinion: The Law of Defensiveness
chapters.sourcePressure: This law turns persuasion into ego management: direct identity threat produces resistance, so influence starts by confirming self-opinion before asking for movement.
chapters.coreMove: Lower ego threat by affirming the person's chosen self-image before introducing the change they would otherwise defend against.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating this as flattery or soft wording instead of removing the identity threat that blocks truth.

chapters.title: Change Your Circumstances by Changing Your Attitude: The Law of Self-Sabotage
chapters.sourcePressure: This law is about perception and usable freedom: attitude filters what people notice, attempt, and persist with, so constriction quietly sabotages options.
chapters.coreMove: Find the constricted attitude that is narrowing your options, then make one expansive action that reveals usable freedom.
chapters.commonMisread: Turning the law into positive thinking instead of showing how attitude changes perception, action, and opportunity.

chapters.title: Confront Your Dark Side: The Law of Repression
chapters.sourcePressure: This law says disowned traits do not disappear; they leak through projection, overreaction, moralizing, contradiction, and scapegoating.
chapters.coreMove: Treat projection and overreaction as evidence of a disowned trait, then integrate the energy instead of acting it out sideways.
chapters.commonMisread: Making the shadow theatrical darkness rather than ordinary traits the self-image refuses to own.

chapters.title: Beware the Fragile Ego: The Law of Envy
chapters.sourcePressure: This law exposes envy as disguised corrosion: another person's success becomes a wound to the self, especially among peers and near-equals.
chapters.coreMove: Detect near-peer envy by tracking when praise, critique, distance, or concern begins to punish another person's rise.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating envy as obvious jealousy instead of a disguised force that often speaks in support, taste, standards, or concern.

chapters.title: Know Your Limits: The Law of Grandiosity
chapters.sourcePressure: This law keeps ambition and delusion in tension: success, praise, and insulation from feedback swell self-image until proportion fails.
chapters.coreMove: Deflate success-driven fantasy by forcing ambition through feedback, constraint, and scale tests before expansion.
chapters.commonMisread: Attacking confidence or ambition instead of showing how lost proportion turns vision reckless.

chapters.title: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You: The Law of Gender Rigidity
chapters.sourcePressure: This law is about integration, not stereotype enforcement: rigid gender performance narrows people by splitting assertive and receptive capacities into hostile camps.
chapters.coreMove: Recover the disowned assertive or receptive capacity that rigid role performance has made feel forbidden.
chapters.commonMisread: Flattening the law into gender stereotypes instead of freeing a fuller range of human traits.

chapters.title: Advance with a Sense of Purpose: The Law of Aimlessness
chapters.sourcePressure: This law presents purpose as an organizing force that emerges through work, refinement, and recognition of one's strongest line, not instant destiny.
chapters.coreMove: Distinguish true purpose from borrowed or false missions by tracking sustained energy, refinement, and sacrifice over time.
chapters.commonMisread: Turning purpose into inspirational destiny language instead of developmental direction built through work.

chapters.title: Resist the Downward Pull of the Group: The Law of Conformity
chapters.sourcePressure: This law shifts to collective distortion: groups bend perception, spread emotional contagion, punish deviation, and need an organized counterweight to reality.
chapters.coreMove: Create a reality counterweight inside group pressure before belonging, faction, and emotional weather drag judgment down.
chapters.commonMisread: Making conformity a brave-individual sermon instead of studying how groups alter perception and reward court behavior.

chapters.title: Make Them Want to Follow You: The Law of Fickleness
chapters.sourcePressure: This law studies the emotional contract between leader and followers: people want direction, resent dependence, test power, and withdraw respect when authority looks needy or unfair.
chapters.coreMove: Establish authority through steadiness, fairness, and inner authority while follower demands shift and test you.
chapters.commonMisread: Making leadership a popularity lesson or command style instead of the unstable emotional contract authority must manage.

chapters.title: See the Hostility Behind the Friendly Facade: The Law of Aggression
chapters.sourcePressure: This law studies hostile force wearing civilized clothing: delay, ambiguity, moral pose, and passive resistance can preserve plausible deniability while causing damage.
chapters.coreMove: Treat friendly obstruction as an aggression pattern and answer with clear boundaries, documentation, and controlled force.
chapters.commonMisread: Calling every difficult person aggressive instead of identifying repeated damage hidden behind politeness or ambiguity.

chapters.title: Seize the Historical Moment: The Law of Generational Myopia
chapters.sourcePressure: This law widens from interpersonal psychology to historical timing: every generation mistakes its emotional weather for timeless reality, while advantage goes to those who read the spirit of the age.
chapters.coreMove: Read generational mood as historical weather, then adapt timing without becoming trapped by your own cohort's assumptions.
chapters.commonMisread: Turning generational myopia into age stereotypes instead of a timing discipline for reading collective mood and openings.

chapters.title: Meditate on Our Common Mortality: The Law of Death Denial
chapters.sourcePressure: The final law says death denial inflates vanity, triviality, and fear, while mortality awareness clarifies proportion, gratitude, urgency, and real investment.
chapters.coreMove: Use mortality to reprice vanity, delay, and petty conflict so finite time directs attention toward what deserves life.
chapters.commonMisread: Making mortality morbid or inspirational instead of a practical test of proportion and seriousness.
